name: one-answer-per-charge
means: An objection is a charge that stays owed until one disposition answers it: a charge is the same across reviews when its kind, `where` and text match with the changing counts struck; one that stops being reported is carried once as `undisposed`, naming where it was raised; and `dispose` writes its answer once — where the charge stands now, with the finding's own text and `where` — so every copy in every review is answered by it and earlier reviews stay as written.
